newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian tin, lead steady while other metals gain.
newsitem.headline: Indian tin, lead steady while other metals gain.

text.p: Indian tin and lead prices on Tuesday steadied while other base metals extended gains, dealers said.

Tin and lead were steady in nominal activity while other base metals lifted further on the back of an upsurge in the world market which prompted speculative buying while limited arrivals limited offerings.
Nickel rose by 200 rupees at 36,800 rupees per quintal after gaining 100 rupees on Monday.
Copper climbed up by 50 rupees at 13,550 rupees per quintal while zinc rose by 50 rupees at 7,900 rupees and aluminium rose by 25 rupees at 7,525 rupees per quintal.

"Actually, the local market went up on the back of an uptrend in the world market but physical buying here still remained low and trading volume is sluggish," said Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metal Exchange.
